articleBody:
Miami's most anticipated dining event is returning this summer with expanded offerings and fresh momentum. The 25th iteration of Miami Spice Restaurant Month will welcome diners from August 1 through September 30, 2026, featuring participating restaurants serving three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings.

According to Miami Curated, the program now encompasses more than 300 restaurants, a substantial increase that reflects both the program's growing prestige and the expanding appetite for deals during the slower summer season. The addition of a Reserve tier this year marks a significant shift in how the program caters to diners, potentially offering premium experiences alongside traditional mid-range and casual options.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau has long used Miami Spice as a strategic tool to sustain restaurant traffic when tourism typically dips during summer heat and hurricane season. By anchoring the promotion to a two-month window and offering deep discounts on multi-course meals, the program encourages both repeat visits and trial of new establishments. The consistency of the August-through-September timeframe has allowed restaurants to plan staffing and inventory with precision.

The 25-year history of Miami Spice underscores how regional tourism boards can build sustainable, recurring events that benefit entire hospitality ecosystems. What began as a smaller initiative has matured into an institution that diners plan around, similar to how other markets leverage seasonal promotions to smooth demand volatility. The introduction of a Reserve tier suggests organizers are responding to feedback from high-end establishments seeking a way to participate while maintaining pricing integrity.

For restaurants, participation in Miami Spice provides marketing exposure and the guarantee of increased foot traffic during a period when many diners are away or dining less frequently due to summer travel. For consumers, the program democratizes access to restaurants that might otherwise fall outside their regular rotation, driven by substantial savings across three courses.

With over 300 venues now confirmed for the 2026 edition, Miami Spice continues to expand its reach while maintaining the core appeal that has sustained it for a quarter-century.

articleBody:
Miami's bar scene has long offered visitors and locals an array of establishments catering to every mood and occasion. Yet for those seeking the particular allure of old-world elegance and refined hospitality, a curated selection of standout venues stands apart. According to Miami Curated, five bars in particular exemplify the kind of sophisticated atmosphere and attention to detail that define truly memorable experiences in the city.

The feature draws its inspiration from iconic spaces like the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, a landmark venue that has long served as a benchmark for luxury hospitality design. The St. Regis New York, located at the southeast corner of East 55th Street and Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, was originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904 to designs by Trowbridge & Livingston. Now operated by Marriott International and holding both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, the property has maintained its reputation as one of the world's premier luxury hotels. Stepping inside the King Cole Bar is often described as an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was not merely an aesthetic choice but a deeply desired way of life.

In Miami, similar spaces have emerged to cater to a clientele that continues to value refinement and formality. While modern fashion and casual culture have reshaped many aspects of contemporary hospitality, there remains a distinct market for bars that preserve and celebrate the standards of classic elegance. These venues distinguish themselves through careful attention to design, curated spirits selections, and service traditions that hark back to earlier eras of sophistication.

The five bars highlighted in the Miami Curated feature collectively represent venues where elegance continues to live—spaces that reject the race toward informality and instead invest in creating immersive environments where guests feel transported. Each establishment offers its own interpretation of refined atmosphere, whether through architectural detail, period-appropriate furnishings, or the caliber of hospitality extended to patrons.

For travelers and residents alike, such venues offer refuge from the casual norm, providing spaces where dressing well and savoring a carefully crafted cocktail in a sophisticated setting remain not only acceptable but expected. In an era when luxury often emphasizes novelty and disruption, these bars stand as reminders that enduring elegance and timeless design continue to hold their appeal.
